pages.title: How prop firms work, the rules that fail people, and what to check before you pay.

blocks.title: How prop firms work

items.text: You pay a fee and trade a practice account under the firm's rules. Hit the profit target without breaking a rule and you pass. Break one rule and the account ends.
You get a funded account. At most firms this is still simulated trading. The firm pays you a share of the profit it shows. Some firms charge an activation fee here.

After the conditions are met (profitable days, a minimum balance, sometimes a consistency rule), you request a withdrawal. You receive your split. Taking a payout can change your drawdown, so read the payout rules before you request one.

blocks.note: **Most of a firm's income comes from evaluation fees.** Moving to a live account, where it exists at all, is the firm's decision after a review. It is never automatic.

items.text: The most you may lose in one day. Touch it and the day ends; at some firms the account ends too.
The lowest balance your account may ever reach. Touch it once and the account is gone. It comes in three kinds:

sub.label: Static
sub.text: the floor never moves. Easiest to plan.

sub.label: EOD trailing
sub.text: the floor rises only when you close the day at a new high. Intraday dips are ignored.

sub.label: Intraday trailing
sub.text: the floor follows your highest balance at any moment, open profit included. Giving back an open winner raises your floor for good. The tightest of the three.

items.note: Most trailing floors stop rising at a set level (the "lock"). Know where yours locks.

items.text: Limits how much of your total profit can come from your best day. One huge day can block a pass or a payout. **Example: 40% to 55%** at the firms we reviewed, Sept 2026. Check your firm's current rules.

The largest position you may hold. 10 micros usually count as 1 mini. It is a ceiling, not a target. **Example: 3 to 6 minis** on a $50K evaluation across four firms, Sept 2026. Check your firm's current rules.
Some plans ban trading around major releases (CPI, FOMC, NFP) or around a set window. Others allow it. Breaking a news rule can end the account even if you made money.
How many days you must trade before passing or before a payout. **Example: none to 5 days** across firms, Sept 2026. Check your firm's current rules.
The share of profit you keep. **Example: 80% to 100%** at the firms we reviewed, Sept 2026. Check your firm's current rules.
The profit you must leave in the account, or the balance you must stay above, when you withdraw. After a payout, some firms reset or fix the drawdown. Check your firm's current rules.
I have read the firm's official rule pages, not a video or a review site.
I know the max drawdown amount, whether it is static, EOD trailing or intraday trailing, and where it locks.
I know whether there is a daily loss limit, and what happens if I touch it.
I know the max contracts for my account size, and how micros count.
I know the news rules and the times I must be flat.
I know the consistency rule for passing AND for payouts (they can differ).
I know the minimum trading days, the payout conditions, the split and the buffer.
I know every cost: the fee, the monthly charge, the reset, the activation, the data.
I have checked the firm's track record and complaints, and I have saved today's rules (they change).

blocks.title: Risk per trade → MNQ contracts
key: Example accounts; the drawdown amounts are examples, check your firm's current rules.

**How to use:** 1) Risk budget = max drawdown × your risk %. 2) Risk per MNQ contract = stop in points × $2 (MNQ = Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100: $2 per index point, and a 0.25-point tick = $0.50). 3) Contracts = budget ÷ risk per contract, rounded DOWN. If the result is 0, don't take the trade, or use a tighter stop only if your setup allows it.
Cell = risk budget → MNQ contracts at a 10 / 20 / 30-point stop.
10% of the drawdown = 10 full losses before the account ends. 5% = 20. 2.5% = 40.
Never go above your plan's max contracts (10 MNQ usually count as 1 NQ). On a trailing drawdown, don't size up after a winning run — the floor rose too, so your room did not grow.

items: Write down your room: balance minus floor. That number, not your balance, sets today's size.
Check the calendar and mark no-trade times around news.
Set your daily stop (see the card below) in the platform if you can.
Pick your size from the table. Write it down.
Every trade has a stop placed at entry.
Same size on every trade. No adding to losers.
Log each trade as you take it.
On intraday trailing: take partial profit or move your stop. Don't let open profit come back.
Update your room (balance minus the new floor).
Mark every rule you followed or broke. Be honest; nobody else sees it.
Check your best day against the consistency rule.
Write one line on what to repeat and one on what to change.

items.fix: Size from your stop and a fixed 5–10% of the drawdown, using the table above.

items.killer: Revenge trading after a loss. The next trade is bigger and faster.
items.fix: After 2 losses in a row, take a 15-minute break. After the daily stop, you are done.

items.killer: Letting a big open winner come back on an intraday trailing account.
items.fix: The floor already moved up with the open profit. Take partial profit or trail your stop.

items.killer: Holding through news or past the close.
items.fix: Put release times and the close time in your calendar. Be flat 2 minutes before each.

items.killer: One huge day that breaks the consistency rule.
items.fix: Set a daily profit cap below the consistency limit, and stop when you reach it.

blocks.title: Stop for the day when any one is true:
items: I have lost half of my daily loss limit (or 25% of my room, if my plan has no daily limit).
I broke one of my own rules, even once.
I reached my daily profit cap.
I feel the urge to "win it back".
blocks.foot: Stopping keeps you in the game for tomorrow.
